newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia dlr builds base, sits out data dry spell.
newsitem.headline: Australia dlr builds base, sits out data dry spell.

text.p: The Australian dollar settled into a snug range atop 75 cents at the midsession and prepared to sit out another event-less local day.

A vigorous two-way tussle offshore had confirmed the strength of US$0.7475 support for the moment. But equally the lack of a follow through attempt at US$0.7530 resistance showed how reluctant even die-hard supporters were to tempt fate and take it higher in the face of a clear rate cut risk.
A dearth of domestic data -- the dry spell will last another week -- means there is little to react to and should keep the currency coralled until the RBA's board meeting on July 1.
By 12.30 pm (0230 GMT) the local currency had encamped at US$0.7505/10 having climbed offshore to an early US$0.7504/09 from US$0.7475/80 late here Thursday.

On the crosses it recouped a little lost ground on the yen to 85.85/95 from 84.90/00 late yesterday. It benefited from a bounce in US$/yen which saw the U.S. dollar add a yen to 114.40 following a lower than expected U.S. trade deficit for April.

In trade weighted terms the local unit edged up to 57.1 from a previous 56.8 close. There were no domestic data out today and the next official release of note is motor vehicle registrations for May on Friday. -- Wayne Cole 61-2 9373 1800
